thread.title_full: Oak Ridge to build new $6M animal shelter; spring start expected - NewsBreak

author: Donna Smith
title: Oak Ridge to build new $6M animal shelter; spring start expected - NewsBreak
text:
By Donna Smith ,
19 hours ago Construction on a new $6 million Oak Ridge Animal Shelter is expected to begin next spring and be completed 12 to 14 months later.
Oak Ridge Animal Control falls under the Oak Ridge Police Department's Administrative Services Division, which is commanded by Capt. Matthew Tedford. Tedford, who works closely with Animal Shelter Supervisor Officer Matthew Roby, provided information on construction plans for the shelter during anupdate to City Council at its Sept. 28 work session.
The shelter will be located on 2.5 acres at the corner of the Oak Ridge Turnpike and Fairbanks Road. It will replace the current shelter, which opened in 1974 on Belgrade Road. The new shelter will be slightly smaller than originally planned because of higher-than-anticipated costs. The new shelter was originally planned to cost $5 million. Deputy City Manager Tom Pessemier said it was discovered during an early design phase for the project that the costs would be $2 million more than expected, so changes were made to reduce costs and allow for a contingency fund. He said the $6 million includes equipment and allows for a contingency fund for the project.
City Council on July 14 approved the hiring of Knoxville-based Barber McMurry Architects to provide architectural and engineering services for the new shelter at a cost of $315,000.
Tedford said despite the scaling back on the project, the new shelter will still be larger, more modern and efficient than the current shelter. It will also have ample storage for supplies such as pet food. He said the current shelter has an outdoor building for storage, plus whatever indoor space that is available at the shelter.
The new shelter will include:
A total of 11,243 square feet, which includes a covered exterior and sally port area for employees in the shelter truck to bring in animals, which the current shelter does not have. The main part of the new shelter will be 9,670 square feet, which is larger than the estimated 6,000 square feet at the current shelter; 25 kennels for adoptable dogs and 15 for dogs that need to stay in quarantine for a while; These 40 kennels will automatically lift up, he said, allowing for shelter personnel to clean the whole area at once rather than the current practice of removing each dog individually and flushing one kennel at a time with water and scrubbing it, before moving on to the next kennel. A catio (patio for cats), a group play area for cats, and the area where the cats will be kept, called a cattery; Meet and greet areas for potential adopters and the animals; A lobby and reception area; Restrooms in two parts of the building, with shower facility included; Office spaces; Volunteer room; A grooming and laundry area; A medical area for the veterinarian. Tedford said one volunteer animal rescue organization has said it will pay for the catio. Questioned by Council member Chuck Hope about whether all the animal advocacy organizations in the city had been contacted, Tedford said there had been informal discussions but no firm donation pledges. He said one woman in the city left $100,000 through her estate.
City Finance Director Kari Bates told The Oak Ridger that the city will likely issue general obligation notes to pay for the $6 million shelter. She said the amount may be higher than $6 million so as to help pay for other capital projects, such as a new fire station at Briarcliff Avenue and Fairbanks Road to replace the aging fire station No. 2 on the east end of Oak Ridge Turnpike.
As reported in The Oak Ridger , Fire Chief Travis Solomon has said the current station has serious foundation problems and the department has outgrown it. Barber McMurry Architects was hired to provide architectural and engineering services for that project, as well. The cost for the fire station work by Barber McMurry: $335,000.
Elsewhere, officials broke ground June 15 on a new, larger Anderson County Animal Shelter in Clinton. Construction of the new shelter is expected to take about a year, according to information from the county government. The cost is nearly $5.9 million with most of the funds coming from low-interest U.S. Department of Agriculture loan.
The Oak Ridger's News Editor Donna Smith covers Oak Ridge area news. Contact her by email at dsmith@oakridger.com .
